MetaboCensoR

Description 📑

The R package and Shiny App for filtering redundant features in LC-MS peak table and associated .mgf file, available through an interactive GUI or standalone R functions.

  • Read the output peak table from mzMine, xcms, MS-DIAL, and Generic format.
    Check compatibility with input examples.
    • Filter features detected in blank sample group(s) with a widget.
    • Filter Isotopes/Dimers, Adducts, Neutral Loses, In-Source Fragments, Mispicked Ions & Saturated (Ringing) Ions, and generate annotation tables.
    • Filter features by Zero, RSD, D-ratio, Mean, and Min values using selectable logical rules with a widget.
    • Filter peaks by m/z, RT, RMD, AMD bounds and a target peak list to remove/keep with a widget.
  • Compile the final filtered peak table, and filter MGF file according to the final peak table.

💡Learn More: Check out the Tutorial for a full GUI walkthrough.
📖Manuscript: Read our Publication for the detailed methodology and benchmarking reports.
🧪Case Studies: Visit the Examples repository for application and evaluation examples.
💻R Functions: Use standalone functions to run filtering workflows directly in R. Check out the GitHub Pages for details. See the full function reference list, the Functions Intro for a short introduction to available functions and parameters, and the Workflow Vignette for a complete analysis example.

Launch the App 🚀

Shiny Web Deployment
plyush1993.shinyapps.io/MetaboCensoR

Install Locally

if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
if (!require("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("plyush1993/MetaboCensoR", INSTALL_opts = "--no-multiarch", build_vignettes = T)

or

if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("plyush1993/MetaboCensoR")

Run Locally

MetaboCensoR::run_metabocensor()

Alternatively, Windows users can launch the app automatically using a .bat file. After installing R, and MetaboCensoR, edit the batch file so that REXE points to your Rscript.exe.
